title: Palindrome Number
statement: Return true when the integer `x` reads the same forward and backward. Negative numbers are not palindromes.
hints: A negative number has a sign and is not a palindrome.
Reverse the digits and compare. Overflow does not matter if you compare the full reverse.
You can reverse only half the digits and compare the two halves to avoid building a number larger than the input.

approaches.name: String compare
approaches.explanation: Compare the decimal representation with its reverse.

approaches.name: Half reverse
approaches.explanation: Stop when the reversed half catches the remaining half.

editorial: Reject negatives. Reverse the decimal digits of the absolute value and compare. The half-reverse version stops when the reversed suffix has as many digits as the remaining prefix, and handles an odd middle digit by dividing the reverse by 10.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def is_palindrome_number(x: int) -> bool:
    if x < 0:
        return False
    original = x
    rev = 0
    while x:
        x, digit = divmod(x, 10)
        rev = rev * 10 + digit
    return rev == original
